newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit surges after Mahathir warns speculators.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit surges after Mahathir warns speculators.

text.p: The ringgit surged against the dollar in afternoon trade as offshore funds sold the dollar after Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's warning of possible action against currency speculators, dealers said.
At 0730 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6350/400 to a dollar after rising to a high of 2.6310. It was trading around 2.6500 in the morning.
Mahathir said on Monday the government would consider taking punitive actions against speculators.
However, he did not outline what specific measures Malaysia might take.
"Offshore players are reacting negatively to Mahathir's comments. They are liquidating long dollar positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said liquidation of long positions in thin market conditions was sending spot dollar/ringgit tumbling as many were uncertain on what the Malaysian government had under its sleeves.
"The government has got some ideas on what to do but obviously we cannot just publish what we want to do...," Mahathir told reporters.
Dealers said wide spreads of 30 to 50 points exaggerated currency movements.
They expect immediate upside for the ringgit to be capped at 2.6200 to a dollar.
